name: Vandetanib (advanced medullary thyroid carcinoma)
cyclesNote: continuous daily dosing until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; not a fixed cycle count

institution.provenance: ONCOTREE draft protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

histology: advanced / progressive medullary thyroid carcinoma (calcitonin-producing C-cell carcinoma)
supportiveCare: baseline and periodic ECG - vandetanib carries a QT-prolongation risk; correct potassium, magnesium, and calcium before and during therapy and avoid concomitant QT-prolonging drugs.
monitor for diarrhea, hypertension, rash / photosensitivity, and rare torsades / sudden death.
reserve for progressive or symptomatic disease; observe indolent metastatic disease with a calcitonin / CEA doubling-time.
trend calcitonin and CEA as response markers.
monitoring: ECG for QT and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium, calcium)

doseModificationRules.condition: QTc prolongation (e.g. > 500 ms) or grade 3 to 4 toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt for QTc prolongation or serious toxicity; resume at a reduced dose (typical reductions 200 mg, then 100 mg daily) after recovery and QTc normalization. Obtain clinical review. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Vandetanib
drugs.notes: Vandetanib 300 mg PO once daily, continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity, is the standard dose for symptomatic or progressive advanced medullary thyroid cancer (per standard guidelines, general reference; ZETA-trial dose). Reduce to 200 mg for moderate renal impairment or QT / toxicity per labeling. Own wording - not a verbatim source copy.
